behavior: The business overview lists what clients still owe: overdue and partly paid invoices with what is left, and money held for the payer (PLAN 10.5)
acceptance: GET /v1/profiles/{id}/owed returns the profile's invoices the payer can still pay that are past their due date (days late, in UTC days) or partly paid, each with what is left (the amount less what the ledger booked to the owner), and each option with money held for the payer, with the held amount. Order: overdue (most days late first), partly paid, held. Another user gets 403.

The freelancer and merchant overview has an Owed to you panel: one row per item linking to its invoice, the days late, partly paid or held for the payer, and the amount; a total of what is left at 1 USD per stablecoin without held money; an empty state; a failed read with Try again. axe 0 and no sideways scroll at 390 px.
openapi.yaml, docs/backend/api.md and DESIGN.md describe the route and the panel.
notes: 2026-10-17 review pass by reviewer: Pass. No blocking defects. owed.go: the open status filter, UTC day math, daysLate, what is left (amount plus the recipient_payable credits of the current option; no settlement or expiry booking exists for an open invoice), held per option from payer_held, order and profile scoping are correct. HTTP, guard, JSON, openapi.yaml and api.md match the code. Web money math uses bigint, 1 USD per stablecoin and one cut to cents. Unknown kinds are left out. Show all moves focus to row 6. Structure and the invoices -> balances import follow the rules. Kept tests guard money, auth and the contract. I ran backend, web, lint, typecheck and docs-check: all pass. Non-blocking notes: (1) owed.go:49-50: an invoice fully booked but still waiting for the second RPC (detected or partially_paid) stays open, so it can show as overdue or Partly paid with 0 left to pay for a short time; amount > 0 would hide it. (2) invoices.spec.ts:576: toContainText('100.00 USD') also matches '100.00 USDC', so it does not prove the payer-chooses row reads in USD; the screenshot does. (3) lib/invoices.ts:337 owedCents repeats the cents math of usdTotal in balances/lib/balances.ts. (4) api.md:191 says unpaid rows are at most MaxOpen; held rows have no bound until refunds exist. (5) The owed route is not in profileRoutes (profiles_test.go:187) and has no 401 test; its own test checks 403. Events, send and cancel are also missing there. (6) Proof 2 does not show the failed read with Try again; the code has it (owed-to-you.tsx:54).

2026-10-17 review pass by reviewer: Pass on the follow-up commit b8005c2. owed.go now drops rows with nothing left (WHERE amount > 0); held rows are unaffected because their sum is never 0. TestOwedToYou covers a fully booked invoice waiting for the second RPC. The e2e test checks USD and not USDC, and waits for the phone layout before it measures sideways scroll. profileRoutes now lists the owed and send routes. api.md describes the left-out rows in one short bullet. I ran backend tests, lint and docs-check: all pass. One new non-blocking note: the comment at invoices_owed_test.go:63 says the invoice waits as partly paid, but one full deposit from open sets it to detected (ledger.go status()). The test still covers the case. Notes 3, 4 and 6 from the first review stay open and are non-blocking.

2026-10-17 review pass by reviewer: Pass on commit 2c0ac95. Only two test files and tasks.json changed. The Go test comment now says detected, which matches ledger status(). The e2e test installs the owed mock before the first load and loads the overview once. It still proves acceptance 2: rows link to their invoice, days late, held rows without left to pay, USD for a payer-chooses row, the total without held money, Show all with focus, axe 0 and no sideways scroll at 390 px. It passed in the 22:58 verify. The real answer through the web schema is no longer in e2e. The 22:28 and 22:46 runs read it and passed, and the Go test covers the API. Non-blocking notes: (1) The 22:52 run also failed the older phone test at invoices.spec.ts:419. The shared Privy user's rate limit is a suite-level risk, and every overview load now adds one owed read. This change only lowers this test's reads. (2) Notes 3, 4 and 6 stay open. The empty state and the failed read with Try again are in the code but in no test or screenshot.
